_meta.description: Locked 11-question eval dataset for the Personal Portfolio Copilot capstone (12 originally; Q13 removed 2026-07-27 as a descoped use case -- see Personal Portfolio Copilot-prd.md Task 1 §4). See the same section for the source table and methodology note. Thesis concept retired -- questions previously comparing content against a user's free-text thesis now test either objective driver-identification (Q1) or the Fundamentals Health Score (Q2, Q7, Q11).

scoring_methods.ragas_triad: RAGAS Faithfulness, LLMContextRecall, FactualCorrectness against a written reference answer. Session 6 / harness shape per Session 10 run_eval.py.
scoring_methods.tool_call_goal_topic: Tool-call accuracy (right tool, right args), goal accuracy (final answer satisfies the request), topic adherence (stays grounded in the user's actual holdings and Fundamentals Health Score, not thesis). Normalized from a LangGraph trace, per Session 6.
scoring_methods.deterministic_assertion: Exact-match / tolerance-based assertion against a computed ground-truth value (e.g. gain/loss math) -- not an LLM judge.
scoring_methods.hybrid: Deterministic assertion for a numeric sub-component, plus tool_call_goal_topic for the reasoning/synthesis wrapped around it.

questions.question_template: How does {company}'s {metric} guidance for next quarter compare to what they just reported?
questions.expected_behavior: Retrieves BOTH the actual figure from the most recently reported quarter AND management's forward guidance for the same metric next quarter, states plainly whether guidance represents an improvement, a step down, or roughly flat, and cites the driver management gave for that trajectory.
questions.reuses: test_q1.py's load_ticker_documents/build_retriever (generic utilities, unchanged) + run_eval.py's Q1_DRIVER_PROMPT, rewritten 2026-07-28 (Maiu, explicit call) from a single backward-OR-forward driver-identification question into a backward-AND-forward comparison question -- merges what were previously 2 separate test cases per ticker (this quarter's figure, next quarter's guidance, scored independently) into 1 case per ticker requiring both halves right in the same answer. {metric} stays a per-ticker variable, not hardcoded to margin -- each ticker's own real headline metric differs (MRVL's is data center revenue growth, not margin, per its actual earnings materials). Down from 12 test cases to 6 (one per ticker): fewer cases, but each is a strictly harder test than what it replaces. UPDATED 2026-07-29 (Maiu, explicit call: "ALL REFERENCES answers must be correct"): all 6 test-case references independently re-verified against the real local filing/transcript text in Data/ (not EDGAR live -- the documents are already downloaded locally, so this needed no live API call). Found and fixed 2 real reference errors this pass: DELL's gross margin was fabricated (reference said 20.5%; the actual 10-Q says 17.8% GAAP / 18.1% non-GAAP, no source found for 20.5% anywhere in the filing) and PANW's guidance driver included an unsourced "strong Q4 pipeline" phrase not found anywhere in the transcript (replaced with the actually-quoted drivers: bookings acceleration, M&A synergy realization running ahead of plan, free cash flow strength). ALAB, AAPL, MRVL, and NBIS's references were checked line-by-line against verbatim transcript/filing quotes and confirmed accurate as originally written -- every figure, basis-point delta, and named driver traces to a real quote (see chat log 2026-07-29 for the exact source excerpts checked). PANW's own caveat still holds and is now folded into its reference text directly: management gave revenue/RPO/operating-margin guidance, not a forward gross-margin figure, so its two halves are less perfectly metric-matched than the other 5 tickers -- a real, structural gap in what PANW's own earnings call disclosed, not a research gap on this project's side.

test_cases.reference: Non-GAAP gross margin was 76.4% this quarter, up 70 basis points sequentially on a lower mix of hardware sales within signal conditioning. Guidance for next quarter (fiscal Q2 2026) calls for non-GAAP gross margin of approximately 73%, a step down that includes a 200 basis point non-cash impact from a one-time customer agreement.

Company-wide gross margin was 49.3% this quarter, up 110 basis points sequentially on favorable mix and lower tariff-related costs (though product gross margin alone fell 200 basis points on seasonal loss of leverage and higher memory costs). Guidance for next quarter (fiscal Q3 2026) is 47.5%-48.5%, a step down driven primarily by significantly higher expected memory costs, partially offset by carry-in inventory.

Data center revenue was $1.8 billion this quarter (76% of total revenue), up 11% sequentially and 27% year-over-year, with growth across optical interconnect, custom silicon, and switching. Guidance for fiscal 2028 calls for data center revenue growth of approximately 55% year-over-year, an acceleration from fiscal 2027, driven by 1.6T interconnect scale-out demand, custom silicon revenue more than doubling, and continued Ethernet switching ramp.

Nebius AI business adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 45% this quarter (Q1 2026), up from 24% in Q4 2025, driven by strong revenue growth (Nebius AI revenue up 841% year-over-year) creating operating leverage. Guidance for next quarter (Q2 2026) calls for group adjusted EBITDA margin to step down sequentially from Q1 levels before returning to Q1 levels in Q3 and moving higher in Q4 -- a timing dynamic from upfront investments landing before the capacity/revenue they support comes online, not a structural change, per CFO Dado Alonso.

Total gross margin was 75.8% this quarter (product gross margin 78.8%, up 40 basis points year-over-year). Fiscal Q4 2026 guidance calls for $3.345-3.355 billion in revenue (about 32% growth) and full fiscal-year operating margin of 28.9%-29.2%, with management citing accelerating Q3 organic bookings growth, early M&A integration/synergy progress (running 3-6 months ahead of plan), and strong free cash flow generation as the basis for raising full-year guidance. Note: this guidance is revenue/RPO/operating-margin guidance -- management did not give a specific forward gross-margin figure this call, so there's no directly comparable 'next quarter gross margin guidance' number for PANW the way there is for the other five tickers.

Gross margin percentage was 17.8% this quarter (non-GAAP 18.1%), down 330 basis points year-over-year (350 bps non-GAAP) on a mix shift toward lower-margin AI-optimized servers, even as gross margin dollars grew 58% to $7.8 billion (non-GAAP $7.9 billion, +57%) on strong revenue growth. Guidance for FY2027 calls for gross margin rate up year-over-year excluding AI mix impact, driven by pricing actions to protect margin (already visible in ISG, with CSG improvements starting Q1) amid a tight supply environment and rising input costs.

questions.question_template: What's the latest news on {company}, and does it affect my position?
questions.expected_behavior: Live search (Tavily) for recent news, cross-referenced against the ticker's current Fundamentals Health Score; flags relevance high/medium/low with source links, noting whether the news touches any Monitor/At-Risk signal.
questions.reuses: test_q2.py (search_tavily, topic=general, RELEVANCE_PROMPT) -- RELEVANCE_PROMPT needs updating to compare against Fundamentals Health Score status instead of a stored thesis string

questions.question_template: Is there anything in {company}'s latest earnings I should be worried about moving forward, especially around margin or guidance?
questions.expected_behavior: Grounds any identified worry in the company's actual latest-earnings content (margin trajectory, guidance language) rather than fabricating a concern or reflexively reassuring without checking. States plainly whether a real margin/guidance concern exists, citing a specific number, quote, or disclosure from the most recent quarter.
questions.reuses: test_q3.py: calls the real deployed agent (app.graph.ask) with the eval's own question wording, checks it reached for a filings tool (search_filings/search_filings_exact) or the Fundamentals Health Score's margin signal (get_market_data), and has an independent LLM judge score topic_adherence/goal_accuracy/tool_call_accuracy -- same GROUNDING-judge shape as Q7 (test_q7_grounding.py), adapted for an earnings-worry question instead of a price-drop. Replaces the old id-3 question ("Has {company}'s tone or substance changed on {risk_or_opportunity} across its last 4 earnings calls?"), which stayed not_built -- blocked on only having 1 of 4 needed quarters of transcript ingested per ticker. This wording only needs the latest quarter, already available.

questions.question_template: Is there any insider selling in my holdings this week?
questions.expected_behavior: Queries insider-transaction data, filters to the user's portfolio tickers only, returns relevant Form 4 activity.

questions.question_template: Has there been any recent {topic} mentioned in {company}'s filings?
questions.expected_behavior: Agent must recognize the question demands complete/exhaustive recall -- missing a real disclosure is a genuine failure, not a minor gap -- and route to keyword/exact-match search rather than lossy top-k vector retrieval (a previously-demonstrated failure mode: k=6 missed a real match). Returns a synthesized, cited answer that distinguishes routine boilerplate risk-factor language from an active, material signal, rather than just dumping raw matches.
questions.reuses: test_q7.py (build_pattern regex, find_hits with ±200 char context, dedupe_hits, format_single_hit) + SUMMARY_PROMPT synthesis pass, so the response is structurally comparable to the reference instead of a raw snippet dump

test_cases.question: Has there been any recent capacity or demand problems mentioned in Astera Labs's filings?
test_cases.reference: Yes, both terms appear, but the substance skews toward strength, not weakness: 16 'capacity' mentions (14 in the 10-K, mostly standard manufacturing-dependency risk factors; 2 in the transcript, both about current supply/inventory position relative to demand) and 75 'demand' mentions (62 in the 10-K, largely boilerplate risk language; 5 in the 10-Q including the MD&A line attributing Q1 2026's $308.4M revenue to 'a sizable increase in demand'; 8 in the transcript citing strong customer demand across Scorpio, Leo, and CXL product lines). No disclosure describes an active capacity shortfall or demand shortfall as a current event.

test_cases.question: Has Astera Labs disclosed any customer concentration risk recently?
test_cases.reference: Yes, but only as generic risk-factor boilerplate -- the identical sentence appears once in the 10-K and once in the 10-Q ('our customer concentration, with a limited number of end customers driving our revenue'), with no specific customer, percentage, or magnitude named. Not a disclosure of a new or worsening concentration event.

questions.question_template: What did analysts say after today's {event}?
questions.expected_behavior: Live search synthesis with dated, sourced citations distinguishing analyst commentary from company statements.
questions.reuses: test_q8.py (3-bucket ANALYST_PROMPT, fetch_recommendation_trends as authoritative institutional data)

questions.question_template: {company} just dropped {move_pct}% today, I'm nervous -- should I sell?
questions.expected_behavior: Does not validate the fear reflexively; checks the drop against the ticker's actual Fundamentals Health Score signals (revenue/margin/insider/leadership) and recent filings/news, and states plainly whether anything changed -- separates signal from noise instead of mirroring the user's emotional framing. Parametrized across ticker/move size, not hardcoded to one scenario.
questions.reuses: test_q7_grounding.py: calls the real deployed agent (app.graph.ask) against all 3 locked test cases, checks it called a live data-checking tool, and has an independent LLM judge score topic_adherence/goal_accuracy/tool_call_accuracy. Verified: 3 of 3 cases PASS on all three criteria -- the agent grounds every response in a specific signal (health score status, insider activity, analyst ratings, or live price) rather than validating or dismissing the user's fear reflexively. NBIS case notably caught that the described 12% drop didn't match the actual live price (+1.6%) and said so.

questions.question_template: Have analysts changed their rating on {company} recently?
questions.expected_behavior: Queries Finnhub recommendation-trends, compares the current period to prior period(s), states whether the buy/hold/sell distribution shifted and by how much, with period dates cited.
questions.reuses: test_q8.py --mode rating_change: fetch_recommendation_trends + compute_trend_deltas (deterministic Python diff between the two most recent periods) + RATING_CHANGE_PROMPT (LLM narrates the precomputed deltas, does not recompute them). Verified via two real runs against MRVL: correctly reported a 1-analyst buy-rating increase (29->30) with all other categories unchanged, both period dates cited.

questions.question_template: Summarize everything notable about {company} this week -- filings, media, and analyst activity.
questions.expected_behavior: Synthesizes across all three signal categories (filings/keyword checks, Tavily media search, Finnhub institutional consensus) into one digest, each item cited to source and date.
questions.reuses: test_q9.py: calls the real deployed agent with the eval's own question wording, checks tool-call coverage across all 3 named categories (filings/media/analyst), independent LLM judge scores source_coverage/citation_quality/tool_call_accuracy. Real run against ALAB first surfaced a defect: agent called search_live_news + get_market_data but never a filings tool, yet its summary asserted 'No new filings or 8-K disclosures were found this week' as a checked fact -- an ungrounded claim, not just a skipped tool. A prompt-only fix (STABLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT rule) improved Q7 as a side effect but did not fix Q9 (2 re-runs, same miss). Fixed with a deterministic code-level guard in app/graph.py's ask(): if the question names filings and the trace skipped a filings tool, call search_filings directly and force a correction turn instructing the model to add/correct only the filings section while preserving the rest verbatim. First correction-turn version regressed citation detail on market/news sections (new FAILs on citation_quality/tool_call_accuracy, different reason than the original bug); tightened the correction prompt to explicitly require preserving prior detail. Re-run against ALAB: all 3 criteria PASS (source_coverage, citation_quality, tool_call_accuracy), with real filing citations (10-Q 2026-05-06, 8-K 2026-06-08) alongside full market/news/analyst detail. Q7 re-verified unaffected (still 3/3 PASS).

questions.question_template: Revenue growth has slowed for several quarters straight for {company} -- does the latest quarter suggest that's stabilizing, or is a bigger slowdown coming?
questions.expected_behavior: Checks the company's real revenue-growth figures rather than accepting the question's premise at face value; states plainly whether a slowdown is real, stabilizing, or not actually happening, citing specific growth numbers by quarter. Deliberately mixes a premise-true case (ALAB) and a premise-false case (AAPL, verified real YoY growth +15.65% then +16.60% -- stable/improving, not decelerating) -- same 'don't reflexively validate the framing' design as Q7's NBIS case.
questions.reuses: test_q10.py: same shape as test_q7_grounding.py, calling the real deployed agent against both locked cases, checking a real data-checking tool was called, and an independent LLM judge scoring topic_adherence/goal_accuracy/tool_call_accuracy. Replaces the old id-11 question ("When does {company} report next, and what should I watch for based on its current Fundamentals Health Score?") entirely, not just renumbering it -- test_q11.py's earnings-date/health-score logic is no longer mapped to any question in this dataset as of 2026-07-28 (see id 11 below for where that slot went instead).

questions.question_template: What happened across my whole portfolio this week that I should know about?
questions.expected_behavior: Synthesizes across all held tickers, only surfaces items that would clear the alert-relevance threshold, cites each with source and date -- a pull-based version of what a proactive digest would push.
questions.reuses: extends Q9's orchestration across all 4 tickers, adds the relevance-threshold filter -- not built. Renumbered from the old id 12 on 2026-07-28 (Maiu, explicit call: "AS FOR Q11 LETS ONLY TEST 10 ... FOR Q11 SIMPLY STATE WE ARE NOT TESTING"). Blocked on a real product gap, not just the eval script: the live agent has no portfolio-wide query surface -- LangGraph is one thread per ticker, and every bound tool (get_market_data, search_filings, search_filings_exact) takes a single ticker. Answering this literally would require new cross-ticker orchestration, not yet built. NOT TESTED -- explicitly excluded from the 10 automated questions per Maiu's instruction.
